AE+SE to provide checklist, security docs, and schedule deep dive to scope benchmark.

transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Jared, Maya, Liam - can you hear us ok?
[00:05] Jared Kim: Yeah, all good. Sorry we had to reschedule earlier. We're the infra/security crew at Halcyon, so this is mainly to understand options for an air-gapped on-prem deployment.
[00:12] Maya Ortiz: Hi, quick note, we have strict no-egress, everything has to be reviewed by compliance.
[00:15] Priya (SE): Great, thanks. We'll walk through Redwood Private on-prem flow and then drill into the offline update story and hardware. Quick intro: Alex handles commercial and I'll handle technical.
[00:27] Alex: High level — Redwood provides hosted, dedicated, and private on-prem. For customers that need air-gapped, we offer a private deployment package with a control plane that can be offline and signed update bundles.
[00:35] Liam Patel: When you say 'signed bundles' can you explain flow? We can't allow internet to the racks. No pull from cloud.
[00:44] Priya: Right, typical flow is: Redwood builds release artifacts, we sign them with an enterprise key, then customer lifts them into their environment via removable media, or via internal transfer. The on-prem control plane validates the signature before applying. We call it the offline bundle flow.
[00:58] Jared: Ok so we do a 'sneakernet' essentially. Who holds keys? We need HSM, FIPS 140-2.
[01:05] Priya: Customers can integrate with their KMS/HSM. Redwood supports HSM backed keys for signing verification or we can work with a shared trust model. We'll document options in the security pack.
[01:18] Maya: Compliance will want audit trails. Are audit logs captured locally? Tamper evidence?
[01:25] Alex: Yes audit logs are local and can be sent to your SIEM. We'll provide logging of update operations, user actions, and model loads. We'll include the retention and log formats in the pack.
[01:33] Priya: Quick question on hardware — do you have a list? GPU types, counts? That drives which model variants we can run.
[01:40] Liam: We're consolidating. Current racks have mix of A100 40GB, couple A100 80GB, and two older A40s. No H100s yet. NVMe is limited to 3TB per node.
[01:51] Alex: That's helpful. Important to note older cards and less NVMe affect KV cache and max context sizes. We can suggest quantized models and recommend batch sizing to hit latency SLOs.
[02:04] Maya: Latency SLOs — our apps need < 500ms p50 for short chat interactions, but for bulk jobs we can tolerate higher.
[02:11] Priya: With A100 80GB we can do fairly high context and decent throughput; A40s will limit throughput and memory. We may recommend model sharding or running smaller sequence lengths. Also, continuous batching can help but depends on traffic patterns.
[02:26] Jared: Are there options to fall back to hosted if capacity is exhausted? We can't have egress.
[02:31] Alex: For strictly air-gapped customers, we can't route to hosted. But there are hybrid patterns — e.g., private with controlled egress for specific functions — however that requires compliance approval. We'll map possibilities.
[02:45] Liam: Driver versions are a thing; our nodes run CUDA 11.6, some newer models need 12.x. How much flexibility on builds?
[02:53] Priya: We ship runtime bundles compiled against specific CUDA/toolkit combos. For air-gapped we'll provide a runtime image for your CUDA version or work with you to upgrade drivers. We'll note any unsupported combos.
[03:05] Maya: Encryption at rest and in transit — we need E2E encryption and keys managed by us.
[03:11] Priya: Supported. We can use customer-managed KMS for model keys and data keys. For HSM-backed keys we have integrations; we will include KMS/HSM integration patterns in the docs.
[03:22] Jared: What about telemetry? We need minimal telemetry out.
[03:26] Alex: By default Private on-prem can run with telemetry disabled; we can provide an offline bundle with telemetry off. For support we can provide signed logs snapshots upon request.
[03:37] Speaker 1: (inaudible) ...
[03:41] Liam: Licensing and SOW — what's typical for pilot? We don't want long commitments initially.
[03:48] Alex: We typically do a short pilot for 4-8 weeks with a limited capacity license. We'll provide pilot pricing and a sample SOW.
[03:55] Maya: Security review — do you have SOC2, ISO docs we can share with compliance?
[04:00] Alex: Yes, we'll attach SOC2 Type II summary, ISO overview, and a technical security pack describing architecture, signing, and audit logs.
[04:08] Priya: On performance: we should scope expected token/sec for your typical queries and we can map to node counts. Do you have QPS expectations?
[04:17] Liam: For chat we expect 10-20 QPS during peaks with short prompts; batch inference for analytics might be 100s of requests but offline.
[04:25] Priya: Ok with A100 80GB a small pool of 4 nodes could handle that for medium models if we use quantized FP16/INT8 and enable KV caching. For A40s might need more nodes or reduced model size.
[04:40] Jared: KV cache — we call it KV cash in our notes lol. How persistent is that? We need to ensure cache doesn't leak across tenants.
[04:49] Priya: KV cache is per-model per-tenant and isolated. We'll describe cache lifecycle and eviction policies. Also options for persistent NVMe backed cache vs in-memory.
[04:59] Alex: Another point — operator experience. We provide a private console for route configs, rollout policies, and per-model dashboards. For air-gapped customers, the console can be operated locally.
[05:12] Maya: Can we do RBAC and SSO? We use SAML and Okta.
[05:17] Priya: Yes SAML/Okta is supported; RBAC is configurable. We'll include sample configs.
[05:23] Liam: What about model updates — e.g., when we want to update to a new LLM, is there a compatibility matrix?
[05:29] Priya: We'll provide a model catalog and compatibility table per runtime bundle. Model onboarding for air-gapped will be a signed model artifact that you ingest. We can also provide a validation harness for local testing.
[05:41] Alex: Let's talk failure modes — if a node goes down, how is failover handled?
[05:45] Priya: The runtime supports smart routing and automated fallback within the private cluster. For graceful degradation, you can route to smaller model variants if latency spikes. We'll document canary rollouts and A/B rollout patterns.
[05:58] Maya: Audit: can we get an example of log format so compliance can validate ingestion?
[06:02] Alex: Yes, we'll include log schema examples.
[06:05] Jared: Anything on physical security? We have racks in a third-party colocation with limited access.
[06:10] Priya: Physical security is customer controlled. We'll provide hardening guidance for nodes, disk encryption, and restricted access best practices.
[06:19] Liam: Performance testing: can Redwood run a benchmark in our environment? We prefer to run the tests ourselves but want Redwood scripts.
[06:26] Priya: We'll hand over the perf harness and synthetic workloads. If you allow, we can run remote assistance via screen-share, but no outbound agent runs.
[06:36] Speaker 2 (Customer): ... (crosstalk)
[06:40] Maya: Licensing detail — do we need to license models separately? Some models have model-licensing constraints.
[06:47] Alex: Model licensing varies by model. For open models we include them; for proprietary ones we license accordingly. We'll call out any specialized license fees.
[06:55] Priya: Also quantization — INT8/FP16 reduces memory and NVMe needs but can affect quality. We'll show regression numbers on sample prompts.
[07:05] Jared: If we want to run larger LLM (>30B) on our hardware, any recommendations?
[07:10] Priya: For >30B you typically need 80GB+ GPUs and NVMe for offload; with your mix, 40GB A100s might work with heavy quantization and offloading but perf will be impacted. We can recommend distilled models or smaller families.
[07:25] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps...
[07:28] Alex: Action items: we'll send security pack, pilot pricing and SOW, Priya will set up the perf harness and schedule deep dive. Halcyon will share hardware inventory and compliance checklist.
[07:40] Maya: Sounds good. Also can you include a sample signed bundle verification flow diagram in the pack?
[07:45] Priya: Yes, diagram and sample commands for validation.
[07:49] Jared: Any competitors we should be aware of? We spoke with Replicate and another vendor.
[07:54] Alex: Replicate, Anthropic and Cohere were mentioned earlier; differences are mostly around ops tooling and enterprise controls. We'll include a short comparison table.
[08:05] Liam: Great. If we can get the docs in a week, we'll aim to do pilot by end of month.
[08:11] Alex: We'll target that. Thanks everyone.
[08:15] Maya: Thanks.
[08:18] Priya: Bye.
[08:20] (call ends)
